Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2607; unblamable:--that cannot be condemned.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in Paul's instruction to Titus about sound speech: Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. The word is unblamable — speech so sound that no accuser can find a fault in it.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse about unblamable speech carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Paul's standard, that the gospel's best defence is a tongue its enemies cannot fault.
